requirements.evidence: Contract is essentially complete: enums (app/Enums/TicketStatus.php:5-8, app/Enums/TicketChannel.php:5-9), InactiveQueueException (app/Exceptions/InactiveQueueException.php:7), Queue fillable/casts/relations (app/Models/Queue.php:11-37), Entity::queues (app/Models/Entity.php:46-49), Ticket casts/nextCode/call (app/Models/Ticket.php:29-129), action with DB re-read, row lock and retry (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:27-60), migrations with cascade FKs, unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_tickets_table.php:20-28), factories (database/factories/QueueFactory.php:22-35, database/factories/TicketFactory.php:23-37). Edge cases handled: malformed codes (app/Models/Ticket.php:80-86), >999 growth (app/Models/Ticket.php:126-129), stale/inactive queue (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:47-51), negative priority (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:29-31), single call and authorization (app/Models/Ticket.php:95-116). One stated rule is only partly honoured: deleting the newest ticket reuses its number because nextCode is 'last remaining code + 1' (app/Models/Ticket.php:72-86), while the task says deleting a ticket does not reuse its number.

conventions.evidence: Docs and changelog kept in sync (docs/business-rules.md:70-89, docs/database-schema.md:532-543, CHANGELOG.md:9); migrations have reversible down() (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_queues_table.php:30-33); the domain write lives in App\Actions\IssueTicket as required (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:32-60); mass assignment is set deliberately with the Fillable attribute (app/Models/Queue.php:11, app/Models/Ticket.php:14). Deviation: authorization is a hand-rolled membership check rather than a policy/gate (app/Models/Ticket.php:95-99), while conventions require authorization to go through app/Policies/.

security.evidence: Issuance re-reads the queue under a row lock instead of trusting the passed model (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:47-51); calling authorizes the acting user against the ticket's entity before any write and leaves the ticket unchanged on failure (app/Models/Ticket.php:95-99, tests/Feature/Queue/TicketCallTest.php:32-54); writes that bypass model events are limited to the whitelisted call fields (app/Models/Ticket.php:104-116); fillable is restricted on both models (app/Models/Queue.php:11, app/Models/Ticket.php:14); input is typed (int priority, TicketChannel enum) and enums are persisted (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:27-60). No unvalidated input, unsafe output or secret exposure.

tests.evidence: Pest coverage of the whole change: issuance/defaults/negative priority/inactive and stale queue/retry (tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php:15-108), code allocation and malformed codes (tests/Feature/Queue/TicketCodeTest.php:12-77), schema/uniques/cascades (tests/Feature/Queue/QueueSchemaTest.php:14-47, tests/Feature/Queue/TicketSchemaTest.php:12-33), write-once matrix (tests/Feature/Queue/TicketWriteOnceTest.php:11-55), call happy path, outsider and cross-entity denial, double call (tests/Feature/Queue/TicketCallTest.php:12-81). Weak spots: the retry test inserts the rival row inside the same transaction, so the rollback removes it and the retry recomputes A001 instead of proving an externally committed collision yields A002 (tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php:72-94); deletion of the newest ticket is untested (tests/Feature/Queue/TicketCodeTest.php:42-51).

simplicity.evidence: Lean, direct implementation: one code path for allocation shared by factory and action through the creating hook (app/Models/Ticket.php:43-45), DB::transaction plus a small retry loop instead of a sequence table (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:33-41), existing User::membershipFor reused for authorization (app/Models/Ticket.php:97), no service/repository layer, no speculative abstractions.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with clear names and docblocks (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:21-60, app/Models/Ticket.php:57-129), the mutable-field list is named and self-documenting (app/Models/Ticket.php:22), the call uses a conditional update with an explanatory comment (app/Models/Ticket.php:104-116), no dead code or debug output; style matches sibling files.

scope.evidence: The diff only adds queues/tickets domain code, tests, and the required doc/changelog updates: app/Actions, app/Enums, app/Exceptions, app/Models, database/factories, database/migrations, tests/Feature/Queue, docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, CHANGELOG.md. No HTTP, Livewire, totem API, call-next selection or unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: nextCode returns the highest remaining code + 1, so deleting the newest ticket reuses its number (e.g. delete A003 from A001..A003 and the next is A003), while the task states that deleting a ticket does not reuse its number; the added docs explicitly acknowledge the reuse, so the behaviour is intentional rather than accidental.

Call authorization is a hand-written membership check instead of a policy/gate, but conventions say authorization always goes through app/Policies/ and the domain action/authorization path should follow that.

The retry test inserts the rival ticket inside the same transaction, so the rollback deletes it and the retry allocates A001 again; it exercises the catch/retry branch but does not prove that a committed concurrent collision produces the next code (A002).
Only deletion of a middle ticket is tested; the documented behaviour for deleting the newest ticket (number reuse) has no test, so the disputed requirement is unverified.

review.summary: The change adds the queue/ticket persistence, enums, exception, models, factories and the IssueTicket action, with write-once and single-call semantics, and updates both docs and the changelog. The implementation is clean and covers almost every requirement, but deleting the newest ticket reuses its code (against the task's wording), authorization bypasses the project's policy/gate convention, and the retry test does not prove allocation after a real collision, so the PR is approvable with those fixes/nits.
